\section[proibido]{proibido — forbidden, not allowed}

\label{lesson:PT-C382-proibido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for optional, then the Portuguese for the obligation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: proibido}
\textbf{proibido} — \textquotedblleft{}forbidden, not allowed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
É proibido fumar no restaurante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Smoking is not allowed in the restaurant.}
\end{quote}

The participle of \emph{proibir}. \emph{Entrada proibida} — no entry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{proibido} is the participle of \emph{proibir}, from Latin \emph{prohibēre} \textquotedblleft{}to hold back, to forbid\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{habēre} \textquotedblleft{}to have, to hold\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proibido}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proibido}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{proibido}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for optional, then the Portuguese for the obligation, then say \emph{proibido} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does proibido mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Forbidden, not allowed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tolerar]{tolerar — to tolerate, to put up with}

\label{lesson:PT-C382-tolerar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the obligation, then the Portuguese for forbidden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tolerar}
\textbf{tolerar} — \textquotedblleft{}to tolerate, to put up with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não tolero barulho depois da meia-noite.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not put up with noise after midnight.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A tolerância} — tolerance.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tolerar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tolerāre} \textquotedblleft{}to bear, to endure, to sustain\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolerar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tolerar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tolerar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the obligation, then the Portuguese for forbidden, then say \emph{tolerar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does tolerar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To tolerate, to put up with\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[autorizar]{autorizar — to authorise, to allow (officially)}

\label{lesson:PT-C382-autorizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for forbidden, then the Portuguese for to tolerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: autorizar}
\textbf{autorizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to authorise, to allow (officially)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O diretor autorizou a visita de estudo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The head teacher authorised the school trip.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A autorização} — the permit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{autorizar} comes from Medieval Latin \emph{auctōrizāre} (EtymDB), built on \emph{auctor} \textquotedblleft{}author, guarantor\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{augēre} \textquotedblleft{}to increase\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{autorizar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{autorizar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{autorizar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for forbidden, then the Portuguese for to tolerate, then say \emph{autorizar} again

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[violar]{violar — to break, to violate (a rule, a law)}

\label{lesson:PT-C382-violar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to tolerate, then the Portuguese for to authorise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: violar}
\textbf{violar} — \textquotedblleft{}to break, to violate (a rule, a law)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O motorista violou as regras de trânsito.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The driver broke the traffic rules.}
\end{quote}

Also, in a grave sense, to rape; for rules many speakers prefer \emph{infringir} or \emph{desrespeitar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{violar} comes from Latin \emph{violāre} \textquotedblleft{}to treat with violence, to violate\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), through Old Portuguese \emph{violar}; it is built on \emph{vīs} \textquotedblleft{}strength, force\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{violar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{violar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{violar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to tolerate, then the Portuguese for to authorise, then say \emph{violar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[a violação]{a violação — the violation, the breach}

\label{lesson:PT-C382-violacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to authorise, then the Portuguese for to break.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a violação}
\textbf{a violação} — \textquotedblleft{}the violation, the breach\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Isso é uma violação da lei.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{That is a breach of the law.}
\end{quote}

In a grave sense also rape; \emph{violação de direitos} — breach of rights.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{violação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{violātiō} \textquotedblleft{}injury, profanation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{violāre} \textquotedblleft{}to treat with violence\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{vīs} \textquotedblleft{}force\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a violação}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a violação}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a violação}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to authorise, then the Portuguese for to break, then say \emph{a violação} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Revisão dos capítulos 375–382}

\label{lesson:PT-R382-revisao-375-382}



\begin{quote}
Say the Portuguese for the secondary school and to attend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the secondary school, to attend, the absence, the list of marks, the school subject
  \item the faculty, the first-year student, the enrolment, the semester, the tuition fee
  \item the lecturer, the thesis supervisor, the scholarship, the master's degree, the doctorate
  \item to revise, the class notes, the textbook, to learn by heart, the test
  \item to fail, to pass, the assessment, the average, the bachelor's degree
  \item the minister, the political party, the parliament, to elect, the voter
  \item the rule, the regulations, compulsory, optional, the obligation
  \item forbidden, to tolerate, to authorise, to break, the violation
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The secondary school? (\textbf{a escola secundária}.) To attend? (\textbf{frequentar}.) The absence? (\textbf{a falta}.) The list of marks? (\textbf{a pauta}.) The school subject? (\textbf{a disciplina}.) The faculty? (\textbf{a faculdade}.) The first-year student? (\textbf{o caloiro}.) The enrolment? (\textbf{a inscrição}.) The semester? (\textbf{o semestre}.) The tuition fee? (\textbf{a propina}.) The lecturer? (\textbf{o docente}.) The thesis supervisor? (\textbf{o orientador}.) The scholarship? (\textbf{a bolsa de estudo}.) The master's degree? (\textbf{o mestrado}.) The doctorate? (\textbf{o doutoramento}.) To revise? (\textbf{rever}.) The class notes? (\textbf{os apontamentos}.) The textbook? (\textbf{o manual}.) To learn by heart? (\textbf{decorar}.) The test? (\textbf{o teste}.) To fail? (\textbf{chumbar}.) To pass? (\textbf{aprovar}.) The assessment? (\textbf{a avaliação}.) The average? (\textbf{a média}.) The bachelor's degree? (\textbf{a licenciatura}.) The minister? (\textbf{o ministro}.) The political party? (\textbf{o partido}.) The parliament? (\textbf{o parlamento}.) To elect? (\textbf{eleger}.) The voter? (\textbf{o eleitor}.) The rule? (\textbf{a norma}.) The regulations? (\textbf{o regulamento}.) Compulsory? (\textbf{obrigatório}.) Optional? (\textbf{facultativo}.) The obligation? (\textbf{a obrigação}.) Forbidden? (\textbf{proibido}.) To tolerate? (\textbf{tolerar}.) To authorise? (\textbf{autorizar}.) To break? (\textbf{violar}.) The violation? (\textbf{a violação}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
